correctness.rationale: A rainbow blade advances all three residues, and no rainbow can be created: a new rainbow has a 2 from an old 1, and if its old triangle had two zeros then both were adjacent to that 1 and advance together. With an active blade the hub rotates. For unordered pairs (00,01,02,11,12,22), direct application of the wing rule gives first times to the phase-appropriate passive pair as (1,4,1,4,-,0), (0,3,-,3,3,3), and (2,-,2,0,2,2) for initial hub 0,1,2 respectively; dashes denote rainbow types. Swapping the peripheral labels commutes with evolution. Without rainbow blades an initial hub 2 yields no 1 after one update (01 is prohibited), then all zero; a hub at 1 leads to this situation at hub 2. A hub at 0 with any 1 advances to 1; with none it rests and all vertices rest after at most one update. This proves the uniform four-step bound. The frozen sharp witness has passive additional blades going 00,00,11,22,00, and a single triangle's ten unordered color multisets give maximum three (001 and 011 attain it). The recurrent active labels fix the periodic state at each hub phase; per phase there are seven choices per inactive blade and one per prescribed orientation, giving all counts and the binomial law. Independent adjacency-based enumeration with first-repeat orbit detection for r=1,2,3,4 confirmed maxima 3,4,4,4, all basin sizes, and counts by active number. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The circulation on an oriented triangle is +3 or -3 for the two rainbow orders and 0 otherwise. A given recurrent orbit therefore has exactly all initial states with its circulation vector (the all-zero vector forces the rest state). Fix the hub color: a ±3 entry gives one ordered pair and a zero gives seven. Summing over three hub colors forces 3·7^(r-k) and choosing the nonzero entries gives binomial(r,k)·2^k. This is mechanical from the known invariant and the exact recurrent skeleton, independent of whether the printed basin count is aggregate.
